Definition: Shaveh-Kirjathajim, a place East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: This name has no verse of its own. Shaveh Kiriathaim is the two-word phrase in Genesis 14:5, where Chedorlaomer smote the Emims in Shaveh Kiriathaim, but the Hebrew text divides it between two other words: Shaveh, the plain, and Kiriathaim, the double city. No token in the Hebrew Bible carries this number, so there is no passage to cite and no verse where the word itself stands.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe honesty about a word that never occurs is better than inventing a use for it. The place is real, and the battle is real, but this entry is a name made from two words, and I hold that saying so plainly is the faithful thing.
